items.review_rationale: Read the full set-diagram colimit construction; a coproduct of sets is disjoint union, but the identification relation and quotient operation are distinct constructions. Used the ordinary indexed-category colimit target rather than an unrelated topological coproduct.

references.phrase: disjoint union of the sets F(i)

references.context: Set theory: equivalence relation generated by a family of prescribed pairs in the disjoint union
Set theory: quotient set of a set by an equivalence relation

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the entire set-valued limit formula, linked arbitrary indexed products to the general categorical product in Sets rather than the restricted binary Cartesian product, and distinguished subset comprehension and naturality equalities from the universal limit itself.

references.disposition: Elementwise compatibility equations for every arrow of the indexing diagram, not a second non-isomorphic limit construction.

items.review_rationale: Read the whole algebraicity criterion and matched the synonym extension field to the actual existing field-extension meaning, with the algebraic-element definition capturing polynomial vanishing. Kept polynomial-ring evaluation separate for later contextual matching.

references.phrase: every element α∈K satisfies a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in k

references.context: Algebra: polynomial ring k[T] over a field and evaluation at an extension element

references.disposition: Universal quantifier over the extension, not a finiteness or transcendence assertion.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the entire characterization of a Galois algebraic extension and linked precisely its algebraic, separable and normal prerequisites, without adding a spurious primitive-element or Galois-group dependency.

references.phrase: both separable and normal over k
references.disposition: Conjunction of two distinct requirements on the same algebraic extension; no additional Galois-group condition is introduced by the wording.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the complete irreducible-polynomial criterion for normality, preserving the irreducible-polynomial and complete-splitting conditions without incorrectly identifying ordinary irreducibility with separability or linking to the splitting-field construction itself.

references.context: Field theory: irreducible polynomial over the base field k, not necessarily separable

references.phrase: splits completely into linear factors over K
references.context: Field theory: polynomial splitting as product of linear factors over an extension field

references.disposition: A polynomial root is an element satisfying the polynomial equation; the hypothesis is conditional, not a request for a distinguished primitive element.

items.review_rationale: Inspected every qualifier of the purely inseparable field-extension criterion: algebraicity, prime positive characteristic, and element-dependent Frobenius-power exponent. Linked the existing field-characteristic meaning, but did not infer a converse or separability requirement.

references.disposition: The p-power condition with an exponent depending on α is given explicitly; do not mistake it for finite extension degree or separable roots.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the whole separability definition, identified separable irreducible minimal polynomials via the no-multiple-roots criterion and linked algebraic closure in the absolute sense, avoiding the distinct relative-algebraic-closure meaning.

references.disposition: Universal quantification over algebraic elements of the extension; it does not require the extension itself to be finite.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the entire fibred-groupoid representability criterion, distinguished equivalence in the 2-category of categories over C from an ordinary set-valued representable functor, and preserved the overcategory C/X as an unassigned construction.

references.context: Category theory: overcategory or slice category whose objects are arrows into X

references.phrase: there exists an object X of C
references.disposition: Existence of a representing object, not an assertion that the fibred category is representable by a scheme.

items.review_rationale: Read the locally ringed-space definition, linking the ambient topological space and the local-ring stalk property while retaining the sheaf-of-rings and stalk-construction prerequisites; no scheme-specific local-affine condition is imposed.

references.context: Algebraic geometry: sheaf of rings on a topological space

references.phrase: stalk at every point of X
references.context: Sheaf theory: stalk of a sheaf obtained as colimit of sections over neighborhoods

references.disposition: Universal quantification over stalk localness at each point, not just generic or closed points.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the full morphism definition, separating continuity, sheaf morphism, induced stalk homomorphisms and the stronger locality condition on homomorphisms; an ordinary unital ring map alone is not mistaken for a local ring homomorphism.

references.context: Sheaf theory: morphism of sheaves of rings compatible with the continuous underlying map
Sheaf theory: stalkwise homomorphisms induced by a morphism of structure sheaves
Commutative algebra: ring homomorphism between local rings carrying the maximal ideal preimage to the source maximal ideal
